summary: Jeremiah writes letter to exiles from Jerusalem to Babylon: thus says Yahweh build houses dwell, plant gardens eat fruit, take wives give sons daughters etc, seek peace of city where I caused you to be carried captive for in its peace you shall have peace, for I know thoughts I think toward you says Yahweh thoughts of peace not evil to give you hope and future, you shall call upon me and go pray I will listen, you shall seek me and find when you search with all heart, I will be found and turn captivity and gather. As for false prophets saying no exile, etc.
whyItMatters: Most quoted for hope — for I know thoughts I think toward you thoughts of peace to give future and hope, plus seek peace of city where you are exiled. Guidance for living in exile, seeking welfare of city.

keyVerses.text: Seek the peace of the city where I have caused you to be carried away captive, and pray to Yahweh for it; for in its peace you will have peace.”
keyVerses.why: Seek peace of city where exiled — welfare of Babylon is your welfare.

keyVerses.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
keyVerses.why: Most quoted — thoughts of peace, hope and future.

keyVerses.text: You shall seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
keyVerses.why: Seek with all heart and find.

questions.question: What does 'seek peace of city where I caused you to be carried captive' mean?
questions.answer: Exiles wanted to stay separate, perhaps revolt or just wait. Jeremiah says build houses dwell, plant gardens eat, marry, multiply, not decrease, and seek shalom of city where carried exile, pray to Yahweh for it, for in its peace you have peace. Counterintuitive: pray for and contribute to welfare of enemy capital Babylon that destroyed Jerusalem. For diaspora living in modern cities, model of engaged presence not isolation, seeking common good even while distinct.

questions.question: What does 'I know thoughts I think toward you thoughts of peace not evil to give you hope and future' mean in context of exile?
questions.answer: Written to people who lost city, temple, king, in exile wondering if God abandoned. False prophets said quick return, Jeremiah says 70 years (long). Then says I know thoughts I think toward you — makhshavot thoughts, plans, intentions — peace not evil, to give you hope (tikvah) and future (acharit — later, end). Not promise immediate rescue but long-term future. Often applied individually, originally communal promise to exiles that exile not end. Hope not from circumstances but God's thoughts. Next verses: you will call pray I will listen, seek find when search with all heart, I will be found and turn captivity.

glossary.def: Welfare, flourishing, wholeness of city where you are exiled, pray for it.
Makhshavot shalom not raah, to give tikvah hope and acharit future.
